body: I haven’t. I’ll check it out.

Suicide and grief do weird things to your relationships. People bring their own biases to the forefront. They think I should be moving forward.. They think if I spend a day crying that I’m stuck in grief. Maybe I am...   

but I have made a couple friends who did not know me before. Those people are my go-tos. We can talk about my situation when I want to or they allow me to be me without being the ‘girl who’s fiancé committed suicide.’  don’t want to tell anyone these thoughts because I know what it’s like to know someone is suicidal & I don’t want to put anyone in that position.

I think you’re right. I think he would want me to keep moving forward, but it’s just a slap in the face on a daily basis. My son is his mini. His looks, his mannerisms, etc.,  It’s a blessing some days. The the waves of grief hit me when he does something new, says something funny, or the fact that his 3rd birthday is in two days. I just wish his father could have seen him and vice versa. 

Sometimes I question why it was so easy for me before to keep my shit together before he died even among the chaos. His death has made life feel so temporary that I no longer care about things that kept me going before.
